items.quote: tl asks "Paano naaamoy ng Philippine crocodile ang biktima sa tubig?" (how does it SMELL its prey) but the tl answer gives a different mechanism: "may espesyal na mga butas sa ulo na nakakaramdam ng galaw ng biktima" — the en original is "How does the Philippine crocodile sense prey underwater?" / "sensing pits ... that detect vibrations from prey", i.e. vibration-sensing, not smell.

EN answer: "a sucker-like disc on its head" -> TL: "may parang suso sa ulo". 'Suso' is Tagalog for snail (cf. ffct-01834 'bahay ng suso') or breast -- never a suction disc. The child is told the remora has a snail/breast on its head instead of a sucker; the corpus elsewhere uses 'supang'/'sipsip' correctly.

EN_LEAD: "Does a millipede bite when scared?" vs TL_LEAD: "Kumakagat ba ang alupihan kapag natakot?" — "alupihan" is the centipede, a different animal that DOES bite (venomous forcipules); TL_ANSWER never restores "millipede" in Tagalog, it keeps the English word: "Hindi — hindi nangangagat ang millipede". A child reading only the Tagalog learns the false fact that centipedes do not bite.

en "Can one mango flower make fruit by itself?" -> tl "Kaya bang mamunga ang isang bulak ng mangga mag-isa?"; "flower" is rendered as "bulak" (= cotton), not "bulaklak". The answer repeats the error ("ang bulak ng mangga", "iisang bulak lang"), so nothing restores it. Elsewhere in this same bank "bulak" is used correctly for cotton (ffct-08970 "Magkatulad ba ang kapok at bulak?", ffct-15423 "halamang bulak", ffct-16563 "bola ng bulak"), confirming the sense is wrong here.

en_ans: "it's called chewing the cud" -> ans: "tinatawag itong pag-usap". In Tagalog "usap" means to talk/converse (chew is "nguya"); "usap" = chew is Cebuano. The card therefore names rumination "pag-usap" (talking), so the Tagalog gives the child a false term for the process the question asks about ("Bakit ngumunguya ulit ang baka ng kinain na niya?").

en_ans "That's the sharp tang your tongue picks up from acidic foods" -> ans "Iyan ang tikatik na lasa ng mga acidic na pagkain". The tl question states the taste is maasim (sour), but the answer names that taste "tikatik", which in Tagalog means a light drizzle of rain, not a sharp/sour taste; the sourness descriptor the card is teaching is replaced by a word meaning something else entirely.

en_ans "the algae make food through photosynthesis, and that food feeds the coral" -> ans "gumagawa ang algae ng pagkain sa pamamagitan ng photosynthesis, at ito ang kumakain ng coral". The direction is reversed: the Tagalog says the algae/food EATS the coral, while the tl question ("May halamang naninirahan sa coral?") and the English both teach that the algae live inside the coral and feed it. A child learns the opposite, predatory relationship.

en: "Why does this insect look like a leaf?" -> tl: "Bakit parang dahon ang katawan nito?" -- the word "insect" is gone and the Tagalog answer never names the creature either ("Lapad ang katawan nito na may gurlis..."), so a Tagalog-only reader has no antecedent for "nito" and cannot tell what the card is about.

en "What's the difference between frogs and toads?" -- "toads" is rendered as "bakulaw", which in Tagalog means gorilla/ape, not toad (palakang-bukid/tukak). The answer repeats the error: "ang bakulaw ay may tuyo at bukol-bukol na balat at nakatira sa lupa", so a child learns that a gorilla has dry bumpy skin and is the land counterpart of a frog.

en "What is the loudest animal on Earth?" becomes tl "Ano ang pinakamalakas na hayop sa mundo?" -- "malakas" applied to an animal reads as STRONGEST, not loudest (the same batch uses the identical phrase for strength: ffct-05410 "Alin ang pinakamalakas na hayop sa lupa?" = strongest land animal, answer elepante). The tl answer repeats the ambiguous "isa sa pinakamalakas na hayop" and never says tunog/ingay, so a child reading only the Tagalog learns the blue whale is the world's strongest animal -- and that it outranks the elephant. Correct rendering: pinakamaingay / may pinakamalakas na tunog.

en_ans: "Sea urchins explode in number" -> ans: "Bibilib ang bilang ng sea urchin" — 'bibilib' means 'will be impressed/in awe', not 'will increase'; the Tagalog never says the urchin population booms.

en asks "Where do special Philippine animals live?" but tl is "Saan makikita ang mga espesyal na hayop?" — the qualifier "Philippine" is gone, and the Tagalog answer ("Karamihan ay nasa kagubatan, bundok, at protektadong lugar") never restores it, so an endemic-species card reads as a generic worldwide claim.

en_ans: 'estimates air temperature from how many chirps happen per minute' -> ans: 'batay sa bilang ng kuliglig kada minuto' = number of CRICKETS per minute, not chirps (chirp = huni). The tl question asks about 'tunog ng kuliglig' (the sound) but the answer tells the child to count the insects.

en: 'Does the HIP JOINT rattle loosely inside?' -> tl: 'Umuuga ba nang basta-basta ang bola sa socket?'. The body part is gone and the tl answer never restores it ('akmang-akma ang bola sa mangkok') — a child reading only Tagalog has no idea what 'bola sa socket' is a part of.

EN question: "Why not the maya as national bird?" and EN answer "was chosen as our national bird" — the words "as national bird" / "bilang pambansang ibon" appear NOWHERE in the Tagalog. TL question is only "Bakit hindi ang maya?" and the TL answer only says "Pinili ang Philippine Eagle dahil natatangi ito" — chosen for WHAT is never stated, so a child reading only the Tagalog cannot tell the card is about the national bird and cannot answer the question.

en_ans: "change its skin's color and pattern in seconds" -> tl ans: "baguhin ... ang kulay at himig ng balat nito"; 'himig' means melody/tune, so the skin-PATTERN fact is lost and replaced by a nonsense trait.

en "Why does cupping your ear help you hear better?" / en_ans "cupping your hand behind it makes an even bigger funnel" -> tl "Bakit mas malinaw ang tunog kapag tinatakpan mo ang tainga?" and ans "kapag tinakpan mo ito ng kamay": cupping a hand BEHIND the pinna becomes tinatakpan = COVERING the ear, and "behind it" (sa likod) is gone from both question and answer. The Tagalog teaches the opposite of the fact -- covering the ear blocks sound; the funnel explanation in the answer contradicts the covering it describes.

en "What pattern hides under a SEA URCHIN's spines?" -> tl "Anong disenyo ang natatago sa tinik ng TIHIK?". "Tihik" is not a sea urchin: in Tagalog (and Cebuano) tihik = kuripot/maramot, a STINGY person. The Tagalog answer repeats the same word ("sa bilog na balat-bato ng tihik") and never names the animal (salungo/maritangtang/sea urchin), so nothing restores it -- a child reading only the Tagalog is told a miser has spines and a round stony shell. Same wrong word is used corpus-wide (ffct-00230 "Kaya ba ng tihik na igalaw ang mga tinik nito?", ffct-00891 "Ang katawan ng starfish at tihik...").

en_ans "most of the plant is hidden inside its host" -> ans "nakatago ang halos buong halaman sa loob ng inaanay nito". "Host" is rendered as "inaanay", which in Tagalog means termite-eaten / termite-infested (anay = termite). The Tagalog never says "host"; a child reads that the Rafflesia hides inside something eaten by termites, a wrong entity that the card nowhere corrects.

en_ans "making clicking sounds that bounce back to help them find their way" -> ans "gumagawa ito ng tunog na pumipikit-pikit para makahanap ng daan". Two losses: "clicking" becomes "pumipikit-pikit" (pikit = to close the eyes, blinking), a word that means something else entirely and is nonsense applied to a sound; and "bounce back" (tumatalbog pabalik) -- the actual echolocation mechanism -- is gone from the Tagalog entirely, so the child is told the bird makes a blinking sound, not that the sound echoes back.

en "What are you made of?" became tl "Ano ang ginawa sa iyo?" = "What was DONE to you?" The composition sense of "made of" is gone: "ginawa sa iyo" is the passive of "do something to someone", not "made out of". A child reading only the Tagalog is asked what was done to them, then answered "Ang lahat ng bagay, kasama ka, ay gawa sa napakaliit na piraso na tinatawag na atom" — the question and the answer are about different things (correct Tagalog would be "Saan ka gawa?").

en_ans "they are made from clay fired in heat" became tl "gawa ito sa luwad na pinaputok sa init". Wrong sense of "fired": "pinaputok" is the gun/firecracker sense (to make explode/discharge) — the same corpus uses it exactly that way in ffct-23029 "Bakit umaatras ang baril kapag pinaputok ito?" and for lava/paputok. So the card teaches that bricks and tiles are clay MADE TO EXPLODE in heat rather than baked/fired (hinurno/sinunog sa pugon), and nothing in the Tagalog restores the kiln sense.

en asks "What is everything in the world made of?" but tl asks "Ano ang ginagawa ng lahat ng bagay sa mundo?" = "What does/makes everything in the world DO?" (ginagawa ng = made BY / being done by, the agent, not the material). The answer answers a different question: "Lahat ... ay gawa sa kombinasyon ng iilang dosenang elemento lamang" (what things are made OF). Correct rendering is "Saan gawa ang lahat ng bagay sa mundo?"

en "What glues bricks together to build a wall?" became tl "Ano ang dumidikit sa mga TISA ..." -- tisa is chalk (or clay roof tile), not brick (laryo/ladrilyo). The same corpus uses tisa for chalk elsewhere: ffct-19904 "What happens when you drop chalk into vinegar?" -> "inihulog mo ang tisa sa suka", ffct-21205 "dust from chalk or flour" -> "alikabok mula sa tisa o harina". The Tagalog answer contradicts the question by naming a different entity: "inilalagay sa pagitan ng BRICKS o BLOCKS".

en "Why do you feel a cool breeze at the beach during the day?" -> tl "...sa beach tuwing umaga?": "during the day" becomes "tuwing umaga" (every morning). The day/night contrast is the whole teaching point of this sea-breeze card (its pair ffct-15996 is the night/land breeze), and the Tagalog answer ("Mas mabilis uminit ang lupa kaysa dagat...") never restores "daytime" — a child learns the sea breeze is a morning thing.

en "Is an alloy a brand-new chemical substance?" -> tl "Ang aleasyon ba ay isang bagong sustansyang kemikal?": "chemical substance" is rendered "sustansyang kemikal", but sustansya means NUTRIENT/nourishment, not substance (Filipino: sangkap / substansiya — this same bank uses "purong sangkap" for "pure substance" in ffct-15817 and "sangkap" in ffct-16053). The Tagalog answer ("Hindi, isa lang itong halo!") never restores the pure-substance-vs-mixture idea, so the child is asked whether an alloy is a new chemical nutrient.

tl asks 'Paano nasusukat ng spring scale ang timbang?' but ans says 'kung gaano naunat ang bukal nito' - en_ans is 'how much its spring stretches'; 'bukal' is a water spring/fountain, a different entity from the scale's coil spring (all 10 other 'bukal' uses in this corpus are water springs, e.g. ffct-20001 'mainit na bukal' = hot spring). A child reads 'how far its fountain stretched'.

en_ans: "Steam comes from hot water and is safe to breathe" -> ans: "Ang singaw ay galing sa mainit na tubig at ligtas languyin" (languyin = to swim in, from langoy; 'safe to breathe / langhapin' is gone, and the card's whole point is steam-safe-to-inhale vs smoke-not-safe)

en_ans "If we used pure iron or stone, they'd need to be huge to stand" -> ans "Kung purong bakal o bato, kailangan silang sobrang BAGAL para tumindig" (bagal = slow; 'huge' = sobrang laki/kapal — the size fact is gone and the sentence teaches nonsense)

en_ans "stay visible in leaves when chlorophyll breaks down in autumn" -> ans "nananatili sa dahon kapag nawala ang chlorophyll sa TAGLAMIG" (taglamig = winter; autumn = taglagas — wrong season taught)
en "Is rust just dirty iron?" -> tl "Ang kalawang ba ay bakal na naging MALINIS lang?" (malinis = clean, the exact opposite of 'dirty'; the answer never restores 'marumi')

en "How does smoking fish like tinapa keep it from spoiling?" -> tl "Paano pinapanatili ng PANINIGARILYO sa isda tulad ng tinapa na hindi ito masira?" (paninigarilyo = smoking cigarettes; smoke-curing is pagpapausok/pagtitinapa)

en "swims up too fast" / en_ans "ascends too quickly" becomes tl "masyadong mabilis sumalang ang scuba diver" and ans "masyadong mabilis ang pagsalang ng diver". Sumalang/pagsalang does not mean to swim up or ascend (salang = to put over a fire / to undergo), so the upward direction -- the whole cause of the bends -- is gone from the question and is NOT restored by the answer, which repeats the same word. A child reads only that the diver moved fast, not that he rose fast.

tl asks "Paano pinapatay ng CO2 fire extinguisher ang sunog?" (how it PUTS OUT the fire) but ans says "Naglalabas ito ng CO2 para lusugin ang apoy" -- lusugin (from lusog, health/vigour) means to nourish or strengthen, the opposite of en "to smother flames". The Tagalog answer tells the child the extinguisher releases CO2 to FEED the fire, directly contradicting its own question.

en "Why do places near the sea have milder temperatures than inland areas?" becomes tl "Bakit mas malambot ang temperatura sa mga lugar malapit sa dagat?". Two losses: "than inland areas" is dropped and the ans also drops it ("ang mga lugar tulad ng Pilipinas ay mas malambot"), so "mas" has no comparison partner and the child cannot answer what it is milder THAN; and "milder" is rendered as malambot, which means soft to the touch, not moderate in temperature.
en "How much does one carat of a gemstone actually weigh?" -> tl "Gaano katinig ang isang carat ng hiyas?" (katinig = consonant; the weight/heaviness sense is gone from the question)

en: "Ever wonder why puddles disappear without boiling?" -> tl: "Napapansin mo ba na nawawala ang latian kahit hindi kumukulo?" — 'latian' means a swamp/marsh, not a puddle; the answer repeats it ('Ang mga latian ay nagiging singaw...'), so the everyday puddle the lesson depends on is gone and the child is told swamps vanish.

en "Do puddles evaporate on cool days?" becomes tl "Nag-e-evaporate ba ang mga LATIAN sa malamig na araw?" -- latian is a swamp/marsh, a permanent wetland, not a puddle (lusak / naipong tubig-ulan). The Tagalog answer repeats "ang mga latian", so the entity is never restored; the child learns about swamps drying up, not the small rain puddle the card is about.

en "What is frost on mountain grass?" becomes tl "Ano ang HAMOG sa damo ng bundok?" -- hamog is dew/mist, liquid water condensed from vapor, which is the exact opposite of what this card teaches. The Tagalog answer then asserts "Ang hamog ay singaw ng tubig na nagiging solid ice crystals nang direkta" (i.e. dew forms as ice without ever becoming liquid), a false statement about hamog; card ffct-20488 in the same batch correctly uses hamog for "morning dew". Frost is namuong hamog / yelong hamog.

en "What is inside the BUBBLING MUD POTS of Tiwi, Albay?" becomes tl "Ano ang nasa loob ng mga PUTIK NA KAWALI sa Tiwi, Albay?" -- kawali is a frying pan, so the Tagalog names the geothermal feature as "muddy frying pans"; "bubbling", the cue that these are boiling geothermal pools, is dropped and is not restored anywhere in the Tagalog answer. A child reading only the Tagalog cannot tell what object is being described.

Question asks about winnowing harvested palay ("Paano hinahiwalay ng pagwinnow ang inani na palay?"), but the Tagalog answer separates the grain from "magagaan na BALAHIBO" -- balahibo is feathers/body hair, a different entity entirely. en_ans reads "the lighter husks"; rice husk is ipa. The card as written teaches that winnowing rice removes feathers.

en: "Why is the water in Taal Lake heavier than pure water?" / en_ans: "It has a higher density!" -> tl: "Bakit mas makapal ang tubig sa Taal Lake..." / ans: "Mas makapal ito!" -- 'makapal' means thick/viscous, not heavy or dense; the density fact is gone from both question and answer, so the Tagalog-only child learns Taal Lake water is THICK and the answer restates the question instead of explaining it.

Question asks how scientists SEE inside the Earth ("Paano nakikita ng mga siyentipiko ang malalim na loob ng Mundo?"), but the answer says "naaalis nila ang istruktura sa loob ng Mundo" (they REMOVE the structure) where en_ans says "they map the deep structure inside the Earth".

en "wind turbine blade tips" became tl "dulo ng pako ng wind turbine" — pako means nail (or fern), not blade. The answer repeats it ("ang dulo ng mahabang pako"), so nothing restores it; everywhere else in this corpus turbine "blades" stay "blades".

en asks composition: "What is a screw thread really made of?" -> tl asks function: "Ano ba talaga ang GINAGAWA ng tirintas ng turnilyo?" (= what does it DO), but the Tagalog answer gives composition, not function: "ito ay isang mahabang inclined plane na binalot sa isang baras". (Also 'thread' rendered as 'tirintas' = a braid of hair; the same bank renders screw threads as 'sinulid' in ffct-23106.)

en_ans "a north pole and a south pole will PULL toward each other" -> ans "Ang magkasalungat na poles ay nag-aakit! ... magkakadikit dahil NAGTUTULAK sila papunta sa isa't isa". 'Tulak' is push/repel, the opposite of 'hila' (pull); the card asserts attraction and then explains it by pushing, which is exactly the attract-vs-repel distinction the magnetism card is teaching.

en_ans 'used the land breeze before dawn to sail out to sea' becomes 'ang land breeze bago madilim para lumayag papunta sa dagat' -- 'bago madilim' is before NIGHTFALL, not before dawn (madaling-araw/bukang-liwayway). The Tagalog then has them ride the sea breeze back 'sa hapon' (in the afternoon), i.e. returning before they left; the child learns the wrong time of day for the land breeze.

en_ans 'A fast vibrating guitar string has high frequency' becomes 'Mabilis na kumukurap na kuwerdas ng gitara ay may mataas na frequency' -- 'kumukurap' means BLINKING (eyes) / flickering, not vibrating (nanginginig/umuuga). The card's one concrete example of what frequency counts is rendered as a string that blinks.

en "Why does lightning hit the tallest thing around?" -> tl "Bakit ang pinakamataas na bagay ang TINITIRHAN ng kidlat?". "Tinitirhan" is the -han form of tira/tirahan = "is inhabited by / is left leftovers by", not "tinatamaan" (is struck). The striking verb "hit" is gone and the Tagalog answer never restores it: it only says "Pinapili ng kidlat ang pinakamalapit na daan mula sa ulap! Kaya mas delikado ang matayog" - no strike/tama anywhere. A child reads that lightning LIVES IN the tallest object.

en_ans "When the clapper strikes the inside" became tl "Kapag tumama ang batingaw sa loob" — batingaw is a large BELL/gong, not the clapper, so the tl answer to "Paano gumagawa ng tunog ang kampana?" says a bell strikes inside the bell; the striking part (clapper) is gone and the child cannot learn what actually hits the metal.

en "Why does black sand stick to magnets on Camiguin beaches?" -> tl "Bakit dumidikit sa bakal ang itim na buhangin sa mga beach ng Camiguin?" -- "magnets" became "bakal" (iron/steel; the same corpus uses "bakal na pako" for "iron nail"), and the tl answer repeats "Madali itong dumikit sa bakal", so the magnet is never restored.

en "drop a hammer and a feather at the same time on the Moon" -> tl "sabay mong ihulog ang martilyo at pamaypay sa Buwan" -- "feather" (balahibo) became "pamaypay" (a hand fan); the tl answer only says "kahit anong bigat" and never names the feather.

en 'What happens to the rope in a tug-of-war?' -> tl 'Ano ang nangyayari sa lubid sa BATUHAN ng lubid?' — batuhan (bato = to throw stones) names a rope-THROWING contest, not a pulling contest (batakan/hilahan ng lubid); the Tagalog answer contradicts the question by describing pulling: 'Hindi ito gumagalaw kung magkapantay ang HILA, pero gumagalaw ito kapag mas malakas ang HILA ng isang panig'

en 'How do ice skates GLIDE SO SMOOTHLY on ice?' -> tl 'Paano GUMAGALA nang MALINAW ang ice skates sa yelo?' — gumagala = wanders/roams (not glide/dumudulas) and malinaw = visually clear (not smoothly/madulas), so the Tagalog question asks how skates 'roam clearly' on ice; the answer never says the skates glide smoothly, only that the water layer is 'parang madulas na lubricant'

en "reach high coconut flowers" / en_ans "high coconut flower spikes" -> tl "matataas na bulak ng niyog": bulak is COTTON in Tagalog (flower = bulaklak). Corpus-wide check confirms every other card uses bulak for cotton (ffct-15423 "halamang bulak", ffct-16563 "bola ng bulak", ffct-30900 cumulus "parang lumulutang na bulak") and bulaklak for flower (130+ hits). Both the tl question and the tl answer say bulak, so nothing restores the flower.

en_ans "light in the sky near Earth's poles" -> tl "ilaw sa langit malapit sa mga poste ng Mundo". Tagalog "poste" means a post / pillar / lamp-post; the geographic pole is "polo" (Hilagang/Timog Polo). The Tagalog therefore says auroras appear near "the Earth's posts", changing the entity the card is teaching, and nothing in the card restores the correct sense.

en_ans "places close to Earth's north or south poles" -> tl "mga lugar na malapit sa hilaga o timog na poste ng Mundo". Same wrong sense: "poste" = post/pillar, not the geographic pole ("polo"). The card's whole point is WHERE auroras are seen, so the child is left with "near the Earth's north or south post".

en "Where is fog most common in the Philippines?" -> tl "Saan madalas magkaambon..." — ambon is DRIZZLE (light rain), not fog; the answer ("Sa malalamig na lugar tulad ng Baguio") never restores fog, so the Tagalog card is about rainfall, not fog.

en "to make dew or fog" -> tl "mabuo ang hamog o ambon" — hamog=dew is fine but ambon=drizzle; the Tagalog answer repeats "hamog o ambon", so the child learns drizzle forms when air cools to the dew point, which is false.
en "How are fog and dew part of the water cycle?" -> tl "ang ambon at hamog" — fog becomes ambon (drizzle); neither question nor answer ever names fog.
en "What do fog droplets cling to when they form in the air?" -> tl "mga patak ng ambon" — fog droplets become drizzle drops; the answer keeps "sila" so fog is never restored.

tl question "Paano nabubuo ang sedimentary rock?" vs tl answer "...dumidiin nang malakas, at tumatagas!" — en_ans is "harden into rock"; tumatagas means LEAKS/seeps (tumitigas = hardens), so the answer to a how-does-rock-form question ends with the sediment leaking and never becoming rock.

en_ans 'most of it is frozen as ice underground and at the poles' -> ans 'sa ilalim ng lupa at sa mga poste'; 'poste' is a post/pillar (lamppost), not a geographic pole ('polo'). The Tagalog says Mars' ice sits 'at the posts', so the polar-ice fact is lost and replaced by nonsense.

en_ans 'an imaginary line through the north and south poles' -> ans 'isang imahinaryong linya sa hilaga at timog na poste'; 'poste' means a post/pillar, not the North/South Pole ('polo'), so the axis definition a child reads is wrong.

en "What happens to the dirt and rocks when a tectonic plate dives underwater?" -> tl "Ano ang nangyayari sa dumi at bato...": English "dirt" here means soil/sediment, but "dumi" in Tagalog means filth/waste/excrement, so the child is asked about the wrong entity; the Tagalog answer only says the English technical word "sediment" ("Na-scrape ang sediment..."), which does not restore "lupa" for a Tagalog-only reader.

tl question "Ano ang mga deep-focus earthquakes?" (deep = lalim) vs tl answer "Nangyayari ito mahigit 300 km ang layo sa subduction zones"; en_ans says "They happen over 300 km deep". "Layo" is distance, not depth, so the Tagalog turns the defining 300 km DEPTH into 300 km AWAY -- and the next clause "Nararamdaman mo ito sa malayo" reinforces the wrong reading.

en: "How big and flat is our Milky Way galaxy?" -> tl: "Gaano kalaki at kalamig ang ating Milky Way galaxy?" -- "flat" became "kalamig" (how cold); the answer gives thickness ("1,000 light-years lang ang kapal") and never mentions temperature, so the Tagalog question is both wrong and unanswered.

items.pattern: outer solar system->labas ng solar system
items.quote: tl asks 'Aling mga planeta ang pinakamalaki sa ating solar system?' but ans says 'Apat na higanteng planeta ang nasa labas ng solar system' = outside the solar system; en_ans says 'Four giant planets live in the outer solar system' (panlabas na bahagi, not labas).

en_ans says "the next closest star, Proxima Centauri"; the Tagalog drops "next" and says "ang pinakamalapit na bituin, Proxima Centauri" — teaching that Proxima Centauri is THE closest star, which contradicts the same sentence's "Ang Sun ay 150 milyong kilometro ang layo" (the Sun is the closest star) and other cards in this bank (ffct-34975: "ito ang pinakamalapit na bituin sa Daigdig").

en "how much rain a big thunderstorm can drop" / en_ans "A single mature thunderstorm" becomes tl "isang malaking bagyo" in both question and answer. "Bagyo" is typhoon/tropical cyclone (used that way throughout this bank, e.g. ffct-35219 "Nabubuo lang ang mga bagyo sa mainit na dagat"), not a thunderstorm, so the Tagalog teaches that a big TYPHOON drops only 500 million liters / 200 pools — a wrong figure for the wrong phenomenon; "mature" is also gone and the answer does not restore "thunderstorm".

en: "Ever wonder where puddles go on hot days?" -> tl: "...saan napupunta ang mga LATIAN sa mainit na araw?". A latian is a swamp/marsh (a permanent wetland), not a puddle; the Tagalog answer only says "Ang likidong tubig..." and never restores the puddle. A child reading only the Tagalog learns that swamps evaporate away on hot days.

en_ans: "wet, mossy forests that are created by the HEAVY MOUNTAIN RAINS" -> ans: "basang, mamasa-masang kagubatan na nabubuo ng MABUHANGING ULAN". Mabuhangin means SANDY, so the Tagalog teaches that the forest is made by 'sandy rain'; nothing in the card restores 'heavy/malakas'. ('Mossy/lumot' is also flattened to mamasa-masa = merely damp.)

tl asks "Ano ang GINAGAWA SA Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park?" (= what is DONE AT the park - an activity question), but ans answers a composition question: "BINUBUO ITO ng limestone rocks na nabuo mula sa accumulated skeletal remains ng corals!". en was "What is the Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park MADE OF?" - 'made of' became 'ginagawa sa', so question and answer no longer match.

tl asks "Bakit NANATILING MATIGAS ang inner core...?" but ans says "pero PINIPIGILAN ng presyon na MAGING MATIGAS NA BAKAL" = 'the pressure PREVENTS it from becoming solid iron' - the exact opposite of en_ans "the pressure KEEPS IT AS SOLID IRON". The Tagalog answer negates the premise of its own question.

tl asks "Ba't isang solidong bola ng apoy ang Araw?" (presupposes the Sun IS a solid ball of fire) but ans says "Hindi! ... hindi isang solidong bola ng apoy!" — the en was a yes/no question, "Is the Sun a giant ball of fire?", so the Tagalog question now asserts the false premise its own answer denies

tl asks about the "Philippine pygmy fruit bat" but ans calls it "ang malaking bat" (the large bat) — the Tagalog question names a pygmy (tiny) bat while its own answer says it is large, so the card teaches the wrong size for the animal

en_ans "A bowed violin string creates a transverse wave" -> ans "Ang hinipan na string ng biyolin" (hinipan = blown with air; a violin string is bowed/hinahagod ng arko, never blown). The card teaches the wrong way a violin makes its sound, and nothing else in the card restores it.

tl asks "Bakit nakakasira sa ecosystem ang MALIIT na pagbabago sa temperatura o tubig?" but ans states "Ang MALAKING pagbabago ay maaaring sumira sa balanse ng ecosystem." -- the answer asserts the opposite magnitude from the one the question asks about, so a child never learns why a small change matters.

Q asks 'Bakit nananatiling nakatigil ang picture frame sa dingding?' but the answer ends '...ang frame ay nananatiling nakahiga' -- en_ans says 'the frame remains at rest'; 'nakahiga' means lying down, which contradicts a frame hanging still on a wall (cf. dcard-01479 which renders 'stays at rest' correctly as 'nananatiling nakahinto').

en_ans "Its job is to fertilize the female egg cell" -> ans "Ang trabaho nito ay lagyan ng pataba ang female egg cell". Wrong sense: "pataba" is agricultural fertilizer/manure, so the Tagalog says the sperm PUTS FERTILIZER ON the egg cell. Biological fertilization is "pagpapabunga" / "i-fertilize". A child reading only the Tagalog learns a false mechanism, and the question ("Ano ang tawag sa male reproductive sex cell?") never restores it.

en_ans "A ball rolling on the floor has mechanical energy from kinetic alone" -> ans "Ang bolang nagpupulong sa sahig ay may mechanical energy mula sa kinetic lamang"; nagpupulong = holding a meeting/conferring, not gumugulong (rolling), so the Tagalog kinetic-energy example is not a moving ball at all

en "How does a pendulum clock keep time?" -> tl "Paano nagtatago ng oras ang pendulum clock?"; nagtatago ng oras = hides the time, not keeps/measures time, and the answer ("Gumagamit ito ng mechanical energy ng umuugoy na bigat o spring") never restores that the clock MEASURES time

tl "Ano ba ang talagang ginagawa ng lupa?" asks what soil DOES/makes (ginagawa ng lupa = done/made BY the soil), but ans answers composition: "Ito ay gawa sa maliliit na piraso ng nabiyak na bato"; en is "What is soil actually made of?" (should be gawa SA / Saan gawa)

en "How do insects smell and see the world?" -> tl "Paano namomoo at nakikita ng mga insekto ang mundo?"; namomoo is not a Tagalog verb for smelling (reads as namumuo = to form/clot) — the English verb "smell" is gone from the question, which asks the child something unanswerable

en "Is a mushroom a plant?" -> tl "Halamanan ba ang kabute?" — halamanan means garden/plant-bed, not halaman (plant), so the Tagalog question asks whether a mushroom is a garden; the answer never re-states the question's category, it only says fungi absorb food "tulad ng halaman".

tl asks "Paano mo ikukumpara ang density ng dalawang bato?" but the Tagalog answer says "damhin kung alin ang mas mabigat" -- the English "heavier FOR ITS SIZE" is gone, so the answer compares mass, not density, and teaches heavier = denser.

tl asks "Bakit nag-aaccelerate ang mga blade ng ceiling fan?" but the answer says "palaging nagbabago ng direksyon at dahil dito ay BUMIBILIS" -- en "therefore accelerating" becomes "gets faster", so the card claims a steadily spinning blade keeps speeding up, destroying the very point that direction change alone is acceleration.
